meta_title: Integral of √(2ax − x²): NCERT Exemplar Q20
meta_desc: Solve ∫√(2ax − x²) dx from NCERT Exemplar Class 12 Q20 by completing the square, then apply the √(a²−u²) standard formula. Free 8-question quiz.

quiz.title: Completing the Square Under a Root Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on turning 2ax − x² into a² − (x − a)² and applying the √(a² − u²) integral. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Integrating √(2ax − x²) by completing the square

questions.q: Which of these is 2ax − x² written as a completed square?
What is the standard integral ∫√(a² − u²) du?
questions.explanation: The standard form is ∫√(a² − u²) du = (u/2)√(a² − u²) + (a²/2) arcsin(u/a) + C.

questions.q: After writing 2ax − x² = a² − (x − a)², which substitution gives the standard form?
questions.explanation: Put u = x − a, so du = dx and the integrand becomes √(a² − u²).

questions.q: So ∫√(2ax − x²) dx equals which expression?
questions.explanation: Substituting u = x − a back into (u/2)√(a² − u²) + (a²/2) arcsin(u/a) gives ((x − a)/2)√(2ax − x²) + (a²/2) arcsin((x − a)/a) + C.

questions.q: To complete the square of x² − 2ax, what must you add and subtract?
questions.explanation: Half of the middle coefficient is −a, and (−a)² = a², so x² − 2ax = (x − a)² − a².

questions.q: In a² − (x − a)², what plays the role of the constant ‘a’ in the √(a² − u²) formula?
questions.explanation: The expression is a² − u² with u = x − a, so the constant is simply a.

questions.q: For ∫√(6x − x²) dx, completing the square gives 6x − x² = a² − (x − a)². What is a?
Therefore ∫√(6x − x²) dx equals which of these?
questions.explanation: With a = 3 and u = x − 3, the formula gives ((x − 3)/2)√(6x − x²) + (9/2) arcsin((x − 3)/3) + C.

faq.q: Why do we complete the square in ∫√(2ax − x²) dx?
faq.a: The integrand has no ready standard form as written. Rewriting 2ax − x² as a² − (x − a)² turns it into the recognisable √(a² − u²) pattern, which has a known antiderivative.

faq.q: How do I complete the square for 2ax − x²?
faq.a: Factor out the minus sign first: 2ax − x² = −(x² − 2ax). Then x² − 2ax = (x − a)² − a², so the whole thing becomes a² − (x − a)².

faq.q: Which standard formula does this problem use?
faq.a: It uses ∫√(a² − u²) du = (u/2)√(a² − u²) + (a²/2) arcsin(u/a) + C, with the substitution u = x − a.

faq.q: What is the final answer to ∫√(2ax − x²) dx?
faq.a: It is ((x − a)/2)√(2ax − x²) + (a²/2) arcsin((x − a)/a) + C, obtained by substituting u = x − a back into the standard result.
